fullPassage: Should we use language to understand mind or mind to understand language? Analytic philosophy historically assumes that language is basic and that mind would make sense if proper use of language was appreciated. Modern cognitive science, however, rightly judges that language is just one aspect of mind of great importance in human beings but not fundamental to all kinds of thinking. Countless species of animals manage to navigate the world, solve problems, and learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely preserved in the minds of humans. There is no reason to assume that language is fundamental to mental operations. Nevertheless, language is enormously important in human life and contributes largely to our ability to cooperate with each other in dealing with the world. Our species homo sapiens has been astonishingly successful, which depended in part on language, first as an effective contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory through written records.

questions.passage: Should we use language to understand mind or mind to understand language? Analytic philosophy historically assumes that language is basic and that mind would make sense if proper use of language was appreciated. Modern cognitive science, however, rightly judges that language is __________ of mind of great importance in human beings but not fundamental to all kinds of thinking. Countless species of animals manage to navigate the world, solve problems, and learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely preserved in the minds of humans. There is no reason to assume that language is fundamental to mental operations. Nevertheless, language is enormously important in human life and contributes largely to our ability to cooperate with each other in dealing with the world. Our species homo sapiens has been astonishingly successful, which depended in part on language, first as an effective contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory through written records.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ just one aspect(단지 하나의 측면)
det.analysis:
빈칸: 인지과학은 언어가 인간에게 매우 중요하지만 '모든 사고에 근본적이지는 않다'고 본다. 따라서 언어는 정신의 '단지 하나의 측면'이라는 흐름.

① the only source(유일한 원천): '근본적이지 않다'는 뒤 문장과 모순
② the true origin(진정한 기원): 마찬가지로 과장
③ just one aspect(단지 하나의 측면): 정답 ← 'but not fundamental'과 자연스럽게 연결
④ a useless part(쓸모없는 부분): '매우 중요하다'는 앞 흐름과 모순
det.tip: language is ______ of great importance but not fundamental → 정신의 '한 측면'일 뿐

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① cooperate with each other(서로 협력하다)
det.analysis:
빈칸: 언어는 인간 삶에 매우 중요하고, 세상을 다루며 '서로 협력하는' 능력에 크게 기여한다는 흐름. 뒤 문장에서 언어가 '협력적 문제 해결'에 기여했다고 이어짐.

① cooperate with each other(서로 협력하다): 정답 ← 뒤의 collaborative problem solving과 일치
② compete against nature(자연과 경쟁하다): 협력 강조와 반대
③ escape from reality(현실에서 도피하다): 무관
④ depend on instinct alone(본능에만 의존하다): 언어의 역할 강조와 모순
det.tip: our ability to ______ in dealing with the world → 뒤의 '협력적 문제 해결'과 연결 → 서로 협력하다
